name: feigenbaum-inverse-norm-obstruction-fast
authority: Derived variant of feigenbaum_inverse_norm_obstruction. Same objects, same measurements, same assertions; the only change is that the eleven monomial compositions are replaced by re-used powers of the inner series. The frozen original is NOT modified and its evidence.json checker_sha256 stays valid.
question: Can the tail bound on the inverse of the linearised operator be obtained in the weighted l1 norm this thread has used, and if not, what does the measurement say must replace it?
level: External exact rational algebra on the frozen candidate; measurements of operator norms and of the tail action; a negative result with reasons, not an enclosure
domain: The candidate fixed point of the doubling operator frozen at thirty digits, the weighted l1 norm with rho = 1/32, the truncated linearisation at degree six with its exact inverse, and the action of the linearisation on the monomials y^j for declared degrees
quantifiers: Every entry of the truncated linearisation and of its exact inverse
Every monomial degree in the declared list, with the weighted norm of its image computed exactly
Every alternative radius in the declared radius control
acceptance: The weighted norm conversion from the truncated coefficient matrix to the space norm is carried out exactly, closing the third missing bound for the finite block, and the resulting norms are reported as they are
The inner series of the composition is shown to have constant term one and therefore weighted norm greater than one, which is checked rather than argued
The action of the linearisation on y^j is measured for the declared degrees and shown not to decay; the measurement is compared with the growth predicted by the inner series deficit
The folding of high degrees back to low degrees is measured, since it is what the weighted norm penalises and a sup norm does not
A radius control is run so that the obstruction is shown not to be an artefact of the declared radius
No new bound on the inverse is claimed, and the redirection to a sup norm on a disk is stated as the required framework
protected: The five earlier Feigenbaum rounds are frozen and are not rewritten; the candidate and the truncated linearisation are imported from the fourth
A negative result is a result: it is recorded with its measurements rather than replaced by a hopeful derivation
No enclosure of alpha or delta is claimed, and no existence claim is made
No metric, Arakelov, Monge-Ampere, mirror or Calabi-Yau content is introduced
No native Rust witness, library admission or Seal follows from this calibration
residual: This closes the norm conversion for the finite block and shows, by measurement, that the tail bound cannot be obtained in the weighted l1 norm, because the inner series has constant term one and every weighted l1 norm therefore gives it norm at least one. It does not produce any bound on the inverse of the full operator, and it does not construct the sup-norm framework that the next step requires. The measurements are for one declared radius and its two controls, one frozen candidate, and declared degrees.

derived_from.why: the original declares budget.wall_seconds = 600 and runs in ~106 s, of which ~84% is Fraction gcd reduction inside rat_compose; eleven of its twenty-two compositions have a monomial first argument, where compose(y^j, inner) == inner^j
derived_from.equivalence_argument: compose(y^j, g) = g^j by construction of rat_compose; both sides are truncated at degree n at every step, and polynomial multiplication mod y^(n+1) is associative, so the truncated results agree. Verified coefficient-by-coefficient for j = 1, 2, 3, 5, 8 against the original rat_compose.
